resources.string: Samsung stops apps in the background. Settings › Battery › Background usage limits, then remove Ping Up from “Sleeping apps”.
Xiaomi stops apps in the background. Settings › Apps › Ping Up › Battery saver › No restrictions, then turn on Autostart too.
Huawei and Honor stop apps in the background. Settings › Battery › App launch › Ping Up: turn off “Manage automatically” and turn on all three switches.
OnePlus stops apps in the background. Settings › Battery › Battery optimization › Ping Up › Don’t optimize, then lock the app in Recent apps with the padlock.
Oppo and realme stop apps in the background. Settings › Battery › App battery management › Ping Up: allow background activity and auto launch.
Vivo stops apps in the background. Settings › Battery › Background power consumption management › Ping Up › No restrictions, then turn on Autostart in the app settings.
Ping Up has no server and no accounts. What you do in the app stays on your phone or goes, encrypted, to the phones around you. Nothing reaches us.

Your name, your friends (their names, public keys and the last zone they told you), your messages, reports, settings and the pilot metrics. Your encryption key is protected by the phone’s own key store: the Android Keystore on Android, the Keychain on an iPhone. The app makes no cloud backups.

Messages to friends are end-to-end encrypted: the phones they pass through can’t read them. When you scan someone’s code, their phone gets your name and public keys, so it lists you too. Reports are encrypted for the event staff and are anonymous unless you choose otherwise; what you write about how to recognise you is seen by staff only. To find each other, phones broadcast over Bluetooth a code that changes about every quarter of an hour, and tell the phones they connect to a technical ID made from your public key. Your name isn’t in either.

We use it on the phone to know which zone you’re in and what’s nearby. Coordinates leave only in a report or for the friends you choose to share them with, as below. Friends learn your zone when it changes or when they ask, while “Tell friends my zone” is on (in Me); someone who added you only by scanning your code learns it once you confirm them or scan their code too, and a zone sent in a message is seen by everyone in the conversation. The app doesn’t track your location in the background, except while you share it.

It’s off until you turn it on. You pick each friend or group you share it with, for how long (15 minutes, an hour, until the end of the festival day or until you stop it) and how exactly: your exact position, an approximate area of about 100 metres, or just the zone. Your position is end-to-end encrypted for the friends you picked: the phones it passes through and the organiser can’t read it. A friend you share it with may attach the last position you sent them to a lost-person report, which goes to the search team. A friend’s phone keeps only your last position, for at most 2 hours. You can stop it at any time from “Who sees me now” or, on Android, from the notification, and your friend isn’t told. Also in Me you can turn on the automatic answer to “Where are you?”: friends who ask then get your approximate area.
Only for scanning QR codes. No image is saved or leaves the phone.

The Ping Up network works without the internet. The phone uses it in two cases only, both your choice: when you load an event pack from a link, it downloads it from that address; and on organisers’ phones, the mobile network log, off unless turned on, makes a small request every 2 minutes to the address the phone’s system itself asks, to see whether mobile data works: connectivitycheck.gstatic.com on Android, captive.apple.com on an iPhone. As with any request on the internet, the server sees the phone’s IP address.

Report times and network counters are noted on the phone. They leave only when you export them, from Me › Export the metrics, and then without the phone’s ID, names, descriptions or coordinates: the place is only the square of the festival grid, about 50 metres across.

Reports reach the event staff. A lost-person report may carry the last position the missing person shared with the reporter, if the reporter chooses to send it. The control room console keeps a log of the reports it got and what was done about them, and the organiser can export it. From it, the organiser can make an edition report for the emergency services (ISU), insurers or sponsors, with no names, descriptions or coordinates: incidents appear only by type, time and grid square.
No ads, no usage statistics sent anywhere, and we give your data to no one.
How long data is kept and how to delete it

Everything stays on the phone until you delete it. A message that hasn’t arrived within 24 hours isn’t sent again. To delete everything, uninstall the app; on Android you can also go to Settings › Apps › Ping Up › Storage › Clear data. What you already sent stays on the phones that received it.
